0x821BEF30
# TEN OF ELEVEN ARE REACHABLE, and the one that is not is the one that matters.
# 0x82300C20's ONLY caller is 0x82234040 -- the entity-level per-frame function
# that cycle 1371's scan showed reads entity+4912, the live flight model
# pointer, more often than any other function in the image. So 0x82300C20 is the
# camera work of the frame that flies the aeroplane: the gameplay camera.
# And it is BLOCKED for exactly the reason the position integrator is. vrefp and
# vrsqrtefp are specified only to a relative accuracy bound; their exact bits are
# a property of the console. Cycle 1383 refused to model them rather than
# approximate them, and that refusal stands here.
# THE DECISION THIS RECORDS. A bit-exact gameplay camera is not reachable by
# micro-execution. A demo therefore uses a camera of its own, captioned as such,
# exactly as the flight session already states that it produces attitude and not
# position. The alternative -- modelling two estimate instructions and calling
# the result retail's camera -- would put plausible numbers where measured ones
# belong, in the one part of the product a viewer looks at directly.
# WHAT IS STILL WORTH PORTING. The other ten are reachable, and 0x8209B398 (400
# instructions, 14 vector, none of them estimates) and 0x82212BD8 (152, scalar)
# are the two largest. Neither has been read; both are bounded.
